name: Tropical Rainforest
lede: Tropical Rainforest is a dark, slightly blue green named for the biome rather than any pigment, dye or place of manufacture.

sections.title: A landscape word
sections.body:
Our library traces the name only to a Wikipedia color list, which gives no date for when the name was coined [1]. It is a landscape word, the dense green canopy of a tropical rainforest, rather than a material or institution [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[patina-green]], 3.5 units of CIEDE2000 away and described as duller [2]. [[generic-viridian]] sits at the same distance, almost the same, [[blue-green]] at 4.2, also almost the same, and [[blue-green]] at 4.3, also almost the same [2]. Measured in LCH it reads lightness 44, chroma 34, a dark, moderately saturated green [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in just 12 of 23,781 paintings (0.05 percent), rarer than 74 percent of the named colors, as photographed [3]. The earliest dated match is 1881, in a work by Pierre-Auguste Renoir, though the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor and not a first [3]. The latest dated match is 1959, across 10 dated paintings in total [3]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so a color match is not a pigment test [3].
